entries.title: Beauty and the Beast

violence.summary: The Beast has angry outbursts and destroys furniture; wolves attack characters and draw blood; an intense mob-storms-the-castle sequence includes a stabbing and a fatal fall, plus some slapstick and gunfire.

language.summary: Derogatory name-calling includes "lunatic," "loon," "scurvy scum," and "pea brain."

romance.summary: Comedic flirting between Lumiere and a maid implies intimate behavior; Belle and the Beast flirt and share a kiss, with brief romantic references in a village scene.

drinking.summary: A tavern scene shows foamy beer mugs being sloshed around.

handoffNotes: CSM's own review age (6+) is one year above the current catalog CA (5+); reviewer may want to confirm the intended app age.

violence.summary: A chicken is killed offscreen with an axe (the sound is heard), characters face repeated peril including threats of being turned into pies, and while there's cartoonish falling and slapstick, scenes with the farmers turn genuinely dark.

language.summary: British slang like "buggers" and "bum" appears, and an older hen calls Americans "oversexed."

romance.summary: Light flirtation occurs between characters, plus the elderly hen's "oversexed" remark about Americans.

drinking.summary: A rooster character drinks a cocktail from a martini glass and acts visibly intoxicated.

entries.title: Frozen

violence.summary: Elsa's magic accidentally strikes Anna, wolves chase the sleigh, a menacing ice creature and armed antagonists appear, one character faces execution, and a severe magical storm may frighten younger viewers.

language.summary: Trolls call Kristoff a "fixer upper" and note his flaws, while dignitaries call Elsa a "monster," "evil sorceress," and other derogatory names.

romance.summary: Anna quickly develops feelings for Prince Hans and hastily accepts his proposal before genuinely bonding with Kristoff; two kiss scenes occur near the end, and Elsa wears a tight, high-slit sparkly dress.

drinking.summary: Champagne is served at a royal reception.

handoffNotes: The film prominently features parental death as a plot driver -- Anna and Elsa's parents are lost in a shipwreck, with the storm/sinking and resulting mourning depicted -- which may need gentle prose context beyond the slider value.

violence.summary: Kiki nearly falls from her broom during wind gusts and crashes through trees, angry crows attack her, Tombo nearly falls from height but is rescued, and storm scenes may frighten sensitive viewers.

language.summary: Mild name-calling includes "stupid" and "snooty."

romance.summary: Tombo flirts with Kiki -- they ride bikes, blush, and share one hug -- and her cat Jiji falls in love and eventually has kittens with another cat, but CSM marks this category as not present.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a drinking, drugs, or smoking concern.

entries.title: A Little Princess

violence.summary: War scenes depict dead bodies in trenches and explosions, Sara has a scary escape sequence where she nearly falls from height, and a neighbor learns of her son's death in the war.

language.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful language concern.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful sex, romance, or nudity concern.

drinking.summary: Schoolgirls discover alcohol (bitters) in the headmistress's office, and an adult drinks brandy without becoming visibly drunk.

handoffNotes: Significant grief and loss themes: Sara's father is presumed dead on a WWI battlefield and her mother died earlier in her life, leaving her a destitute orphan who struggles with grief and leans on imagination to cope -- this may need gentle prose context beyond the slider value.

violence.summary: Extensive slapstick includes martial arts moves, Kermit is pursued by armed antagonists with gunfire, a scientist threatens a "brain scrambling" device, and there are car crashes, a Muppet near a ceiling fan, dynamite, and kidnapping at gunpoint.

language.summary: Mild insults like "shut up" and name-calling appear, plus mild wordplay jokes.

romance.summary: Kermit and Miss Piggy hug and kiss, including a dream sequence of the two frolicking together; beauty pageant competitors wear one-piece swimsuits.

drinking.summary: Bar scenes show adults with mugs, one character smokes a cigar, characters drink wine with straws, and a song references drinking beer before sleep.

entries.title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs

language.summary: The queen summons her magic mirror by commanding "Slave!" -- a minor but pointed word choice noted by CSM.

romance.summary: The prince kisses an unconscious Snow White, and several songs focus on romantic themes, though overall content is minimal.

drinking.summary: Snow White eats a poisoned apple, which effectively drugs her into unconsciousness.

handoffNotes: CSM's own review age (6+) is one year above the current catalog CA (5+); reviewer may want to confirm the intended app age.

romance.summary: Gentle, understated romantic feelings develop between the two robots and between a human couple.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful sex, romance, or nudity concern.

entries.title: Coco

violence.summary: Day of the Dead imagery includes skeletons that come apart frequently and beheaded/limbless figures; a character is crushed by a large bell (played for humor); characters face chasing and peril including a fall from height; and a character is shown succumbing to poison.

language.summary: Infrequent mild words include "stupid," "dumb," "jerks," "hate," and "bum."

romance.summary: References to a couple's love story and embracing, kissing in a movie-within-the-movie, and a skeleton posed for an artist (played for humor).

drinking.summary: Adult characters drink in a couple of scenes, including a shot in one scene and drinks at a party.

handoffNotes: The film heavily addresses death, grief, and family separation -- a character dissolves into dust and another appears to fade in a tear-jerking climactic sequence, with the story centered on loss of beloved relatives and remembrance traditions -- this needs gentle prose context beyond the slider value.

violence.summary: Cartoonish sequences include Santa wrestling an elf, park rangers chasing Santa's sleigh, Buddy getting hit by a taxi but bouncing back unharmed, and a ferocious-looking raccoon nearly attacking.

language.summary: Infrequent mild profanity includes "pissed," "pee," "hell," "damn," "crap," and "up yours," plus jokes at the expense of a little person character.

romance.summary: Dating and romantic tension between the leads includes one kiss, and a scene shows a woman singing in the shower while Buddy sings from another room, without graphic nudity.

drinking.summary: Two characters spike their coffee with whiskey and become noticeably intoxicated in a comedic scene; wine appears at dinner and a character's burping is attributed to drinking.

violence.summary: Farmers try to kill Mr. Fox with guns, explosives, and kidnapping; a character dies in a knife fight; a rabid-dog confrontation creates tension; and Mr. Fox's tail is shot off, though nothing is graphic.

language.summary: Strong profanity is replaced with the stand-in word "cuss," as in "What the cuss?" and "cluster cuss."

romance.summary: Mr. and Mrs. Fox share embraces and kisses, a rat character alludes to Mrs. Fox's past, and two adolescent foxes flirt and become romantically involved, creating jealousy.

drinking.summary: Adult animals drink hard cider, wine, and champagne at meals without excess; one farmer drinks multiple jugs of cider daily; and pipe and cigarette smoking appears throughout.

violence.summary: Death and torture are constantly threatened and implied; the film opens with a shootout and features crushed/impaled skeletons and the discovery of a frozen dead body.

language.summary: Several instances of profanity include "s--t" and "bulls--t," along with "damn," "goddamn," "ass," and "hell."

entries.title: Home Alone

violence.summary: Frequent slapstick violence builds toward the finale -- falls down stairs, being struck with objects, stepping on nails and glass, burns, and characters knocked unconscious; the protagonist shoots burglars with a BB gun and a movie-within-the-movie shows a character machine-gunned; an imaginary furnace also appears threatening.

language.summary: Profanity includes "s--t," "crap," "damn," "hell," and "bitch," plus sibling name-calling like "disease," "puke," "jerk," and "moron."

romance.summary: Adult characters kiss, the protagonist finds an adult magazine but shows minimal interest, and teens reference "nude beaches" and body-related topics.

drinking.summary: Brief adult drinking and smoking appears, including a Santa-dressed character with a cigarette and champagne on an airplane.

handoffNotes: CSM's own review age (10+) is two years above the current catalog CA (8+); reviewer may want to confirm the intended app age given the elevated language and slapstick-violence content.

entries.title: Little Manhattan

violence.summary: Karate-related combat includes kicking, punching, and tripping; Gabe breaks his hand during board-breaking; a bully throws a dodgeball that non-seriously injures children; and characters fall off a scooter without injury.

language.summary: Only two instances of the word "hell" appear in dialogue.

romance.summary: Young characters kiss (replayed repeatedly in one character's thoughts), adult versions of the characters kiss, the protagonists witness a couple making out on public transit, and two young characters briefly wrestle on the floor.

drinking.summary: Kids drink non-alcoholic Shirley Temples while adult guardians drink wine.

handoffNotes: The film centers on Gabe's parents' separation and divorce (they still live together while dissolving their marriage), which may need gentle prose context beyond the slider value.

entries.title: Matilda

violence.summary: Cartoonish violence mostly from the school principal: a girl is flung over a fence by her pigtails, a boy is tossed from a window, children are placed in "the chokey" (a closet lined with nails and glass), and a boy is struck with a cake plate; a brief reference to suicide also occurs.

language.summary: One instance of "hell" and uses of "oh my God" as exclamations, plus substitute profanity where adults say things like "dog slime" instead of real swearing.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful sex, romance, or nudity concern.

drinking.summary: Adults occasionally drink beer on screen, with Budweiser cans visible.

handoffNotes: CSM notes a brief reference to suicide amid the principal's cruelty toward the children; may warrant gentle prose context given the age range.

entries.title: The Neverending Story

violence.summary: A quick but slightly bloody clash with a snarling wolf, a faceless "Nothing" destroying Fantasia, bullying classmates, a giant rock monster, and the traumatic scene of a swamp swallowing a beloved horse.

language.summary: Name-calling includes "weirdo," "jerk," "chicken," and "nutcase"; an adult calls his wife a "wench."

romance.summary: Two sets of large sphinx statues have prominent breasts with protruding nipples.

drinking.summary: An adult briefly smokes an old-fashioned pipe.

handoffNotes: The film centers heavily on grief and loss: Atreyu's horse Artax sinks into the Swamp of Sadness and dies, a scene many adults recall as traumatizing, and the story explores characters who have given up hope amid overwhelming sadness -- this needs gentle prose context beyond the slider value.

entries.title: Paddington 2

violence.summary: Paddington chases a thief through the streets during a robbery, prison scenes initially feature intimidating inmates, a train chase puts characters in peril, and Paddington nearly drowns but survives; the emotional low point is Paddington crying alone in prison believing his family abandoned him.

language.summary: Only mild expressions like "yellow bellies," "coward," and "weirdo," plus "Oh my God" as an exclamation; no strong profanity.

romance.summary: A couple of marital embraces and quick kisses between the Brown parents.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a drinking, drugs, or smoking concern.

handoffNotes: Paddington's belief that his family has abandoned him while he's imprisoned is an emotionally intense separation/loss beat that may need gentle prose context.

language.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful language concern.

romance.summary: A giant baby's exposed bottom appears briefly.

drinking.summary: One character smokes a cigarette with an ashtray visible, and sake is offered to another character.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful sex, romance, or nudity concern.

entries.title: Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope

violence.summary: Laser blaster firefights, lightsaber duels, and spacecraft combat occur throughout; minor characters are shot and killed; Darth Vader fatally chokes victims; burnt skeletal remains are briefly visible; a character's arm is severed bloodily; and a garbage compactor scene has walls closing in on the heroes.

language.summary: Two uses of "damn" and two uses of "hell," plus a derogatory reference to "sand people."

romance.summary: Mild flirting and the suggestion of crushes between lead characters; one character kisses another on the cheek.

drinking.summary: Characters briefly visit a space cantina that serves otherworldly beverages and substances to smoke.

handoffNotes: Significant grief and death themes: Princess Leia witnesses her entire home planet Alderaan destroyed along with everyone on it, Luke discovers his aunt Beru and uncle Owen burned to death, and Obi-Wan Kenobi is killed by Darth Vader -- these may need gentle prose context beyond the slider value.
